question: An Infra goods invoice arrived on Saturday with no GRN. Should I chase the site on Monday morning?
gold: Hold it (the system reminds after two working days), but experienced staff wait until Tuesday noon before any manual chase because Infra sites post GRNs in a Monday-morning batch.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: No — hold as NO_GRN; wait until Tuesday noon before chasing
Answer: No — the invoice should be held as NO_GRN with the requester notified automatically, and you should not post it against the PO without a GRN whatever the requester says on the phone. [1] The system sends a reminder after two working days and escalates to the requester's manager after five working days, and the Requester owns resolution of NO_GRN with a target of 5 working days. [1][2] For Arvana Infra Projects, requesters must post GRNs within two working days of receipt. [3] In practice, Infra sites batch their GRNs on Monday morning, so anything that comes in Friday to Sunday is waited on until Tuesday noon rather than chased on Monday. [4][5]
Expert tip: Infra sites batch their GRNs on Monday morning.

question: Arvana Retail Pvt Ltd: PO unit price ₹120 for 500 units; the invoice charges ₹122 per unit. Can the line pass the price match?
gold: No — raise PRICE_VAR. Excess ₹1,080 on a line value of ₹60,000; limit is the lower of 1% (₹600) and ₹500 = ₹500.
answer_text:
Status: answered
Decision: Hold the line — price variance above tolerance
Answer: No — the line cannot pass the price match: the excess of ₹1,000 on the line is above the ₹500 limit, so the line is held with exception PRICE_VAR. [1] A line passes only if the total excess is no more than the lower of 1% of the PO line value and ₹500, and here the limit is ₹500. [1] The held line is sent to the buyer who raised the PO, and the buyer either amends the PO or asks the supplier for a credit note. [1]
